patterns.what_worked: Reading the client source first (wow-ui-source) settled the pink-versus-blue question with citations instead of assumption: Classic Era loads Vanilla/ClassColors.lua (SHAMAN = 0.96, 0.55, 0.73 pink) while TBC/Wrath load TBC/ClassColors.lua (SHAMAN = 0, 0.44, 0.87 blue, identical to the main add-on's SHAMAN_BLUE_COLOR). Building ONE resolver in Core and having all three surfaces call it is what makes 'they agree' a structural property rather than a hope. Every pin was reverted on a copy of the tree and shown to go red.
patterns.what_was_hard: The saved tooltip mode carries no 'the user set this' marker, so the old default and a deliberate choice are indistinguishable - the requested migration cannot be done safely, and the task's own rule says not to override a saved value. A schema bump is not an escape hatch either: initializeDatabase treats schema > 2 as a future schema and force-disables the equipment windows. The character/inspect frame's rendered text is not observable through the mock (anonymous FontStrings), so that surface is pinned structurally rather than behaviourally, and that is stated rather than papered over.
patterns.skill_gap: Two harness traps cost real time and are now recorded in the journal: an `and`/`or` expression truncates a multiple return to one value (the colour helper's green and blue read nil), and a module file that publishes itself on the namespace returns nothing from loadfile.
